questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

Mahesh said to the interviewer, "Sir, I was in charge of the production unit at my previous office."

options.text: Mahesh told the interviewer that Sir was in charge of the production unit at my previous office.
Mahesh told the interviewer that he had been in charge of the production unit at his previous office.
Mahesh told the interviewer you were in charge of the production unit at my previous office.
Mahesh told the interviewer I was in charge of the production unit at his previous office.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 2) i.e. Mahesh told the interviewer that he had been in charge of the production unit at his previous office.**

__
 
• While changing direct speech into indirect speech** said to** is changed into **told**.
 
• And** 'I'** is referred to **Mahesh**, hence, 'I' will be changed into **'he'**.
 
• The tense of the reported speech (here:** Simple past)** would undergo a** backshift **(get changed into** Past perfect) i.e. 'was/were'** would be changed into **'had been' **and** V2 would be changed into V3.**
 
• All these rules are followed in option 2, hence, it will be the correct answer.

NOTE: __When a sentence is converted from Direct speech into Indirect speech:

 
• If the 'reporting verb' is in 'Past tense', the 'Reported speech' would undergo a backshift of tense.
 
• Modal verbs (Will, may, can) would take their past forms (would, might, could).
 
• Pronouns would change according to the subject of reporting verb.​
 
• "said to" will get converted to "told", "asked", "commanded", requested" etc.depending on the tone of the narrator.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. I decided to make a donation to help.**

 
• **'has'** cannot be used with **'I'**, so the given sentence needs improvement.
 
• The past indefinite tense is most appropriate to convey the meaning of the given sentence. Hence, **'I decided'** will be used.
 
• **'to+infinitive'** is the correct choice to used here, hence, **'to make'** will be used in the given sentence.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Today flax is used to make fine linen fabric.

B. The Neolithic man first clad himself with animal skins.

C. He also used flax which had a good fibre for making cloth.

D. But in those days cloth made of flax must have been very rough.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3) i.e. BCDA.**

 
• The only **independent sentence** from the given sentences is** 'B',** hence it will be the** first** sentence.
 
• In the sentence **'C' **the pronoun **'he'** has been used for **'neolithic man'**, hence, it will follow the sentence 'B'.
 
• This sequence i.e.** 'BC'** is given in only option 3), hence, it will be the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The cyclone has damaged several crops.

options.text: Several crops have damaged the cyclone.
Several crops had been damaged by the cyclone.
Several crops are being damaged by the cyclone
Several crops have been damaged by the cyclone.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. Several crops have been damaged by the cyclone.**

 
• The given sentence is in the** present perfect tense**, hence, while converting it into passive voice** 'has/have been' **will be used.
 
• The subject while making the passive voice will be** 'several crops'** which is a plural subject.
 
• Hence, '**have been'** will be used.
 
• In passive voice, **v3** is used.
 
• All these rules are followed in option 4), hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

We will use enamel paint on this wall because it gives a best finish.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• The phrase 'a best finish' should be replaced by 'the best finishing' to make it grammatically correct. The noun 'finish' means 'an end of something' and 'finishing' means 'the act of completing something'. Article 'the' should be used instead of 'a' because the superlative degrees are always followed by the definite article 'the'.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is 'We will use enamel paint on this wall because it gives the best finishing'.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Baskets and carts flooded the street turning it into a mobile market.

B. Hearing their cries people with bags started coming out from their ho uses.

C. Suddenly the street came alive.

D. From one end to the other cries of the vendors rent the air.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• The answer begins with sentence C as it means the street got suddenly busy with activity of many living beings.
 
• 'A' will be the second sentence as it is saying how the street got busy.
 
• Sentence D & B make the paired sentences as sentence D is saying the street was filled with screams of vendors. Sentence B continued saying that hearing the screams of the vendors people started coming out with bags.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence is given in Option 4 'CADB'.**
